title: add input-fragmentation-workload + saliency reporter to exercise tokenizer pathologies
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new workload that synthesizes tokenization fragmentation and a saliency-reporting pipeline to surface token-level cost/latency hotspots; useful for validating tokenizer edge-cases and regression detection.
description:
Summary: Implements a deterministic input-fragmentation workload generator and a lightweight saliency reporter that annotates per-token latency/cost and tokenizer boundary sensitivity. Motivation: Several production regressions were traced to pathological tokenization splits (e.g., long hyphenated identifiers, mixed-script sequences) that trigger worse attention/kernel paths and KV cache miss patterns. Existing benchmark runners do not systematically exercise these cases. This PR introduces a focused workload and a reporter that produces CSV/NDJSON outputs consumable by the perf pipeline.

What this changes: - benchmark-lab/runner/fragmentation_simulator.go: new runner that synthesizes sequences with controlled fragmentation parameters (split density, subtoken variance, script-mix ratio, primer overlap). Includes deterministic RNG seeding to make runs reproducible. - benchmark-lab/reporters/saliency_reporter.py: collects per-request token timing, model-variant fallback notes, and a tokenization boundary score. Exports both human-readable summaries and machine-parsable NDJSON for downstream aggregators. - benchmark-lab/configs/fragmentation_profiles.yaml: presets used in CI (short-identifier-heavy, mixed-script, hyphenation-heavy, adversarial-primer). - benchmark-lab/test/fixtures/fragmented_prompts.json: example prompts used in unit+integration tests. - docs/bench/fragmentation-workflow.md: usage guide and interpretation notes for the saliency metrics. - .github/workflows/bench-frag.yml: CI job that runs the new workload against a small test model (ci-cpu mock) and validates expected metric shape.

Commits: - "init: fragmentation workload generator and interfaces" - "reporter: saliency NDJSON exporter and CSV summarizer" - "tests: fixture prompts and unit tests for tokenizer boundary scoring" - "docs: runbook and examples" - "fix: race in exporter when streaming to Gzip"

Files changed (high level): - benchmark-lab/runner/fragmentation_simulator.go (new) - benchmark-lab/reporters/saliency_reporter.py (new) - benchmark-lab/configs/fragmentation_profiles.yaml (new) - benchmark-lab/test/fixtures/fragmented_prompts.json (new) - docs/bench/fragmentation-workflow.md (new) - .github/workflows/bench-frag.yml (new) - benchmark-lab/runner/runner_test.go (updated, adds integration cases)

Testing and CI: The bench-frag workflow runs a quick smoke of 120 requests with three profiles. The first run hit a flaky timing assertion in runner_test.go (race between aggregator flush and test teardown). I pushed a fix that adds a test synchronization barrier and retried CI. After the fix CI passed on the second run (all checks green). The PR also includes unit tests for the tokenizer-boundary scoring routine and a small golden NDJSON file for schema validation.

Performance notes: The reporter's overhead is intentionally low — the reporter samples 10% of requests by default and aggregates token timing at microsecond resolution; measured overhead in local runs is ~2-3% additional CPU for the runner process at 100QPS workload. The fragmentation workload surfaces p95 token-latency spikes in two profiles (hyphenation-heavy and mixed-script) on the mocked CPU model; these will be used to validate future kernel/attention optimizations.

Review thread (summary): - Diego Ramos: "Can you add a short note in the docs explaining how this workload maps to real customer cases (e.g., code completion, multilingual input)? Also request a toggle in the reporter to disable NDJSON streaming for long runs." -> I added mapping notes to docs and a --ndjson-disable flag in the reporter. - Anika Patel: "Test flakes? please add coordinator barrier to runner_test.go" -> Added a barrier and updated the test to wait for exporter close. - Evan Liu: "Nice work. Can we add a small sanity check that tokenization boundary scoring is robust to different tokenizer vocab sizes?" -> Added a parameterized unit test that runs with two tokenizer mock configs. Approvals: Diego and Evan approved after fixes; Anika requested the barrier change which was addressed.

Follow-ups: - ENG-1199: hook saliency NDJSON into the perf aggregation pipeline for automatic anomaly detection (follow-up PR). - ENG-1184: add GPU-backed CI job to run the fragmentation workload against a small quantized model.

Docs and runbook: docs/bench/fragmentation-workflow.md explains interpreting the token boundary score (0..1) where higher indicates stronger fragmentation impact, and provides example NDJSON outputs and how to visualize token-level heatmaps in the perf dashboard.

Why this PR is safe to merge: changes are additive (new runner and reporter) and tests + CI coverage added. The new CI job is opt-in (bench-frag workflow does not gate main CI) and reporter sampling rate defaults to 10% to avoid undue overhead.

Merge details: Squash-merged into main after approvals and successful CI.

If you want to run locally: 1) go to benchmark-lab/ 2) go build ./runner 3) ./runner --profile=hyphenation-heavy --seed=42 --sample-rate=0.1 4) tail the ndjson file created in /tmp and run the included visualization notebook in docs/bench/ to produce token heatmaps.
merge_details: Squash-merged into main after approvals and successful CI.
